summary.en: The Paris Peace Treaty transferred the Dodecanese from Italy, which had held the islands since 1912, to Greece. Greek administration began in March 1947 and the formal union followed on 7 March 1948. It was the last enlargement of the Greek state.

body_html.en:
Italy had taken the Dodecanese from the Ottoman Empire in 1912 as a pledge during the Libyan war and never gave them back. Lausanne confirmed Italian sovereignty in 1923, and the fascist governors of the 1930s pursued a policy of Italianisation that the islands' Greek majority resisted.

Germany seized the islands after the Italian armistice in 1943 and held them until May 1945. The British military administration that followed handed over to Greece in March 1947, three weeks after the peace treaty had been signed. The union was proclaimed at Rhodes a year later.
